title: Israeli Prime Minister Rejects US-Led Gaza Peace Plan
subtitle: Benjamin Netanyahu demands complete disarmament of Hamas before any military withdrawal, creating a public disagreement with the White House.

summary.en: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has officially rejected a 15-point peace plan for Gaza proposed by US President Donald Trump. The plan aimed to trade a full Israeli military withdrawal for the disarmament of Hamas and other armed groups. Netanyahu insists that Hamas must be genuinely disarmed before any Israeli forces leave the territory. This rejection marks a rare public break between the Israeli leader and his closest international ally. The move comes as both leaders face upcoming elections, adding political pressure to the ongoing conflict.
summary.zh: 以色列總理納坦雅胡已正式拒絕美國總統川普為加薩提出的十五點和平計畫。該計畫旨在以以色列全面撤軍，換取哈瑪斯及其他武裝團體解除武裝。納坦雅胡堅持在任何以色列軍隊離開該領土前，哈瑪斯必須真正解除武裝。此次拒絕標誌著這位以色列領導人與其最親密的國際盟友之間罕見的公開決裂。此舉正值雙方領導人皆面臨即將到來的選舉，為持續中的衝突增添了政治壓力。

paragraphs.en: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has publicly rejected a 15-point peace plan for Gaza proposed by US President Donald Trump. The plan, which was introduced by the US-led Board of Peace in July, aimed to create a path toward long-term stability in the region. However, in a cabinet meeting held on Sunday, Netanyahu made it clear that Israel would not follow the proposal as it is currently written.
paragraphs.zh: 以色列總理納坦雅胡 (Benjamin Netanyahu) 已公開拒絕由美國總統川普 (Donald Trump) 所提出的加薩十五點和平計畫。該計畫由美國主導的和平委員會於七月提出，旨在為該地區的長期穩定創造途徑。然而，納坦雅胡在週日召開的內閣會議中明確表示，以色列不會遵循目前草案中所述的內容。

paragraphs.en: At the heart of the disagreement is the order of events regarding security. The US plan suggested a phased process where Israeli troops would withdraw from Gaza while Hamas handed over its weapons to an international force. In contrast, Netanyahu stated that the Israeli military would not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is “genuinely disarmed.” He emphasized that this must include all heavy and light weaponry, rejecting what he called “fictitious disarmament.” According to BBC News, Netanyahu told his cabinet that Israel knows how to stand its ground, even against its best friends, when it comes to national security.
paragraphs.zh: 雙方分歧的核心在於安全事務的執行順序。美國的計畫建議採取分階段程序，即以色列軍隊從加薩撤離，同時哈瑪斯 (Hamas) 將武器移交給國際部隊。相對地，納坦雅胡聲稱，在哈瑪斯「真正解除武裝」之前，以色列軍方不會進行任何撤軍。他強調這必須包含所有重型與輕型武器，並拒絕了他所謂的「虛假裁軍」。根據英國廣播公司新聞網報導，納坦雅胡告訴內閣，在國家安全問題上，以色列知道如何在即使面對最親密的盟友時，依然堅持自己的立場。

paragraphs.en: The peace plan was intended to build upon an earlier ceasefire—an agreement to stop fighting—that began in October 2025. While that initial agreement allowed for the release of hostages and an increase in humanitarian aid, it left the most difficult issues, such as the future of Hamas’s weapons, for later discussions. Trump’s new roadmap sought to resolve these issues by proposing a transition of power to an independent Palestinian committee. However, Hamas has maintained that it will only hand over its weapons if Israel ends its military actions and withdraws its forces from the territory.
paragraphs.zh: 這項和平計畫旨在延續二零二五年十月開始的早期停火協議。雖然最初的協議促成了人質獲釋與人道援助增加，但將最棘手的問題，例如哈瑪斯武裝的未來，留待後續討論。川普的新路線圖試圖透過提議將權力移交給一個獨立的巴勒斯坦委員會來解決這些問題。然而，哈瑪斯堅持只有在以色列結束軍事行動並從該領土撤軍的情況下，才會交出武器。

paragraphs.en: This rejection highlights the complex political environment surrounding the conflict. Both the US and Israel are approaching important elections, which makes compromise difficult. As reported by The Guardian, Netanyahu is facing pressure from hardline members of his own government who want him to take a tough stance on Gaza. By publicly challenging the US plan, the Israeli leader appears to be strengthening his reputation as a defender of Israel’s security at home, even if it risks damaging his relationship with the White House.
paragraphs.zh: 此次拒絕凸顯了圍繞這場衝突的複雜政治環境。美以雙方都即將面臨重要的選舉，這使得妥協變得困難。據《衛報》報導，納坦雅胡正面臨來自其政府內部強硬派成員的壓力，要求他對加薩採取強硬立場。透過公開挑戰美國的計畫，這位以色列領導人似乎正在鞏固他作為以色列安全捍衛者的國內聲譽，即便這可能會損害他與白宮之間的關係。

paragraphs.en: Despite the rejection, representatives from the US Board of Peace continue to defend the proposal. Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for the board, told Israeli media that the plan remains the “only way forward” to ensure that the violence of the past does not happen again. Mladenov noted that the plan was designed to be a verifiable process, meaning that each stage could be checked and, if necessary, stopped to ensure safety.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管遭到拒絕，美國和平委員會的代表仍持續為該提案辯護。該委員會的高級代表姆拉德諾夫 (Nickolay Mladenov) 向以色列媒體表示，該計畫仍然是確保過去的暴力事件不再重演的「唯一前進道路」。姆拉德諾夫指出，該計畫旨在成為一個可驗證的程序，意味著每個階段都可以進行核查，並在必要時暫停以確保安全。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, the situation on the ground remains tense. According to NPR, Israel still maintains control over a significant portion of Gaza. While the US and Israel continue to hold discussions about how to move forward, there is no clear sign of a breakthrough. Hamas has stated that it remains committed to the original roadmap and has called on international mediators to ensure that all parties follow the agreements that were previously made.
paragraphs.zh: 與此同時，當地的局勢依然緊張。根據美國國家公共廣播電台報導，以色列目前仍控制著加薩的大部分地區。雖然美以雙方持續就如何推進進行討論，但目前沒有出現任何突破的跡象。哈瑪斯表示，他們仍致力於最初的路線圖，並呼籲國際調解人確保所有相關方遵守先前達成的協議。

paragraphs.en: The disagreement also reflects wider tensions in the Middle East. The US is currently working on multiple fronts to bring peace to the region, including efforts to end conflicts in Lebanon and address the war with Iran. The White House is particularly interested in stabilizing the region to help manage global issues like oil and petrol prices. However, as the latest developments show, the different interests of the US, Israel, and Palestinian groups continue to make a lasting peace deal very difficult to achieve.
paragraphs.zh: 這項分歧也反映了中東地區更廣泛的緊張局勢。美國目前正多管齊下以期為該地區帶來和平，包括致力於結束黎巴嫩的衝突以及處理與伊朗的戰爭。白宮特別希望穩定該地區，以協助管理石油與汽油價格等全球性議題。然而，正如最新的發展所顯示，美國、以色列與巴勒斯坦各方之間不同的利益，使得達成持久的和平協議依然困難重重。

paragraphs.en: As the situation develops, the world is watching to see if the US can convince Israel to change its position or if the 15-point plan will be replaced by a new strategy. For now, the path to peace remains blocked by deep disagreements over security, trust, and the fundamental requirements for ending the war.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著局勢發展，全世界都在關注美國是否能說服以色列改變立場，或者這項十五點計畫是否會被新的策略所取代。目前，通往和平的道路仍因對安全、信任以及結束戰爭的基本要求存在嚴重分歧而受阻。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To maintain one's position or refuse to change one's opinion despite opposition.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是一個慣用語，字面上是「站在自己的土地上」，這裡指在壓力下不妥協。文中：Netanyahu told his cabinet that Israel knows how to stand its ground, even against its best friends, when it comes to national security.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To use an existing achievement or agreement as a base for further development.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於商業或計畫，指以某事為基礎繼續推進。文中：The peace plan was intended to build upon an earlier ceasefire—an agreement to stop fighting—that began in October 2025.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Relating to a strict, uncompromising policy or political position.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常形容政治立場，指拒絕妥協的態度。文中：Netanyahu is facing pressure from hardline members of his own government who want him to take a tough stance on Gaza.

keyTerms.definitionEn: In the actual, practical situation or location where events are happening.
keyTerms.noteZh: 指實際發生的狀況，而非理論上的計畫。文中：Meanwhile, the situation on the ground remains tense.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason Benjamin Netanyahu gave for rejecting the US peace plan?

options.A: He believes the plan does not provide enough humanitarian aid to Gaza.
options.B: He disagrees with the proposed sequence of military withdrawal and disarmament.
options.C: He feels the plan was created without consulting the Israeli government.
options.D: He thinks the plan is too similar to the ceasefire agreement from October 2025.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，爭議的核心在於「事件的順序」（order of events）。美國計畫提議以色列軍隊先撤出，哈瑪斯再繳械，但納坦雅胡堅持在哈瑪斯「真正解除武裝」前，以色列軍隊不會撤離。選項 A 文中未提及援助不足；選項 C 與文章提到的「US-led Board of Peace」不符；選項 D 雖然提到 2025 年協議，但納坦雅胡拒絕的主因是安全程序的順序，而非協議內容的相似性。

quiz.question: Based on the article, why might Netanyahu be willing to risk his relationship with the US administration?

options.A: He believes the US is secretly supporting Hamas's demands.
options.B: He wants to prove to the international community that the US plan is illegal.
options.C: He is prioritizing his domestic political standing over international diplomatic pressure.
options.D: He intends to replace the US as the primary mediator in the Middle East.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第四段，納坦雅胡面臨國內強硬派的壓力，且即將面臨選舉。透過公開挑戰美國計畫，他能強化自己作為「以色列安全捍衛者」的形象。這顯示他將國內政治利益置於與白宮的外交關係之上。選項 A 文中無此暗示；選項 B 文中未提及計畫違法；選項 D 則過度推論，文中並未顯示他有取代美國作為調解人的意圖。

quiz.question: In the second paragraph, what does Netanyahu mean when he rejects 'fictitious disarmament'?

options.A: He believes the proposed disarmament is fake or insincere.
options.B: He thinks the disarmament process is too expensive.
options.C: He feels the disarmament plan is too complex to implement.
options.D: He argues that disarmament is not a necessary condition for peace.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在語境中，「fictitious」意指虛構的、假裝的。納坦雅胡強調必須包含所有重型與輕型武器，這意味著他認為美國計畫中原本的方案可能流於形式，無法真正落實解除武裝，因此稱其為「虛假的」（fictitious）。選項 B、C 與成本或複雜度無關；選項 D 與文意相反，他認為解除武裝是撤軍的前提，非常必要。

quiz.question: Which of the following best summarizes the main message of the article?

options.A: The US and Israel have successfully established a new roadmap for peace in Gaza.
options.B: Hamas has agreed to the US peace plan, but Israel continues to block it.
options.C: The peace process is stalled due to fundamental disagreements on security and political interests.
options.D: The Israeli government is planning to cut all ties with the US due to the 15-point plan.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文旨在探討美國提出的和平計畫為何遭到以色列拒絕，並分析了背後的安全疑慮、國內政治壓力及區域複雜性。結論提到和平之路因信任與安全的分歧而受阻，這正是文章的核心主旨。選項 A 與事實不符；選項 B 忽略了哈瑪斯也有自己的條件；選項 D 誇大了兩國關係的破裂，文中僅提到關係緊張，並未提到切斷關係。
